questions.stem: 50 cm³ of hydrochloric acid reacts completely with 5.3 g of sodium carbonate: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. What is the concentration of the HCl? (Mr of Na₂CO₃ = 106)
questions.explanation: Moles of Na₂CO₃ = 5.3/106 = 0.05 mol. From the equation, 1 mol Na₂CO₃ reacts with 2 mol HCl, so moles of HCl = 0.1 mol. Volume = 50 cm³ = 0.05 dm³. Concentration = n/V = 0.1/0.05 = 2 mol/dm³.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of NaOH solution is neutralised by 30.0 cm³ of 0.1 mol/dm³ H₂SO₄: 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. What is the concentration of the NaOH?
questions.explanation: Moles of H₂SO₄ = 0.1 × 0.030 = 0.003 mol. From the equation, 1 mol H₂SO₄ reacts with 2 mol NaOH, so moles of NaOH = 0.003 × 2 = 0.006 mol. Concentration = 0.006/0.025 = 0.24 mol/dm³.
